H1.title: Minutes trend: when his last 3 games averaged 4+ minutes off his usual, project him at his last-3 minutes
H1.label: input fix
H1.notes: From the misses log: calls leaning into a player running above his usual minutes went 6 of 7 (Oct 26-27), but that used the minutes he went on to play. This is the pre-tip version: recent minutes over the usual (the morning file's last 10). It can't fire until players have 5+ games, when the two differ
H1.plain: moves a player's projected minutes to his last-3 average when it runs 4+ minutes off his usual, instead of his usual minutes
H1.adopt_plain: build that minutes trend into the morning Proj

H2.title: Blowout trim (the board's NBA_BLOWOUT): a 30+ minute player whose team is favored by 10+ projects 1 point lower
H2.label: situational
H2.notes: Built into the board's morning Proj (off once ETR's file is in). Scored against the base plus the matchup term, as the board applies it. Re-run of the study (2023-26): favorite stars lose 1 min at 10-12.5 and 2.5-3 at 13+, mostly won back per minute; net of the opponent about -0.5/-1.0 at 10-12.5 and -0.9/-2.2 at 13+ (fit/test). See blowout_study.md. Retired 2026-11-10 (no longer beating the base over its last 14 nights: -0.01, 65 players); taken out of the board's morning Proj. H4, the sliding version, carries the idea forward.
H2.plain: took a point off 30-minute players on teams favored by 10 or more
H2.retired_plain: it didn't help, and the blowout slide, which scales the cut with the spread, carries the idea forward

H3.title: Underdog bench: a player under 20 usual minutes whose team is a 10+ point underdog projects 2 points higher
H3.label: situational
H3.notes: The most consistent effect in the blowout study: +1.4 to +3.3 FP and +2 to +3.5 min at 10+ (fit 2023-25 and test 2025-26); this season so far +2.5 against ETR (n 74). Scored against the base plus the matchup term
H3.plain: adds 2 points to a bench player (under 20 usual minutes) whose team is a 10-point underdog
H3.adopt_plain: raise those bench players in the morning Proj

H4.title: Blowout slide: as H2, but -1 at 10-12.5 and -2 at 13+
H4.label: situational
H4.notes: The study's open question: net of the opponent the 13+ favorites ran -0.9 (fit) and -2.2 (test). Read against H2 on the same players; it only differs at 13+
H4.plain: takes a point off 30-minute players on 10-12.5-point favorites and 2 points at 13 or more
H4.adopt_plain: put that sliding cut into the morning Proj

Q-1.idea: Q push by flag, chance and tier: VALUE or over 70% to play, no push; T1-T2 PRICEY or under 50%, two tiers back; else the current rule (AM no push, PM two back)
Q-1.why: Both Q rules were tested one size fits all; the 11-09 report sends Luka (80% to play) from T1 to T3 in PM. Expected shape (the user's): keep VALUE Q-tags and high-chance stars; push PRICEY or low-chance ones in T1-T2

test.rule: For a player tagged Questionable at the window's record, with p his calibrated chance to play (nba_q_lane fit) and c his combined tier: VALUE or p > 0.70: no push (tier c); else c in T1-T2 and (PRICEY or p < 0.50): two tiers back (min(5, c+2)); else the current rule (AM c, PM min(5, c+2)). Order: the pushed tier, then the button's rank. Graded on 6-drafter decision pairs (ADP within 4, any tiers) with a Questionable player that the rule orders differently from the button; a scratch scored through his swap; positive = the rule beat the button.
test.backtest: Before any forward grading: for Questionable players, the push decision split by flag (VALUE / unflagged / PRICEY), calibrated chance (under 50%, 50-70%, over 70%) and tier (T1-T2 vs T3-T5), in each window: back one and back two against no push, on decision pairs where they differ, points per pair with the 80% range and the evidence label; cells under 40 pairs are 'not enough yet'. 72 cells: by chance alone about 40% of cells with enough pairs would show a lean.

Q-1.plain: Push Questionable players by type: VALUE players and those over 70% to play stay put; in T1-T2, PRICEY players and those under 50% to play drop two tiers; everyone else follows the current rule
Q-1.name: Questionable pushes by type

T2-1.idea: T2 by ADP to about pick 9 (the 1/2 turn), then by the window's projection from about pick 10 to the end of T2
T2-1.why: Brings the money-backed 2/3-turn rule (reach toward the higher projection: RULE for, lift 1.82) into the board. The worry: projection straight lost to ADP across all of T2 in AM (-6.5 per pair, 51 pairs); test whether picks 10+ behave differently

test.rule: Inside T2 at a window's record (ADP: the window's; projection: ours in AM, ETR in PM): a player at ADP 9.5 or earlier (the 1/2 turn) goes ahead of one after it; two at 9.5 or earlier go by ADP; two after it go by the projection. Flag groups as the button (VALUE first, PRICEY last): a pair with different flags keeps the button's order. Graded on 6-drafter decision pairs (ADP within 4) inside T2 that it orders differently from the button; a scratch scored through his swap; positive = the idea beat the button.
test.backtest: Before forward grading: inside T2, projection straight against ADP straight on decision pairs, split by where the pair sits: both at ADP 9.5 or earlier, straddling 9.5, both after 9.5 (picks 10+); AM (primary sample) and PM; points per pair, positive = projection right, 80% range and label (under 40 pairs: not enough yet). Then T2-1 against the button in sample.

T2-1.decide: Per window (2026-11-09): the shadow grades AM and PM apart (T2-1:am, T2-1:pm), and each window's Monday call stands on its own forward read: PM can be adopted on its own even if AM isn't, and the reverse. The backtest suggests PM (ETR beat ADP past pick 10, +3.7 on 75 pairs) and not AM.
T2-1.plain: Order T2 by ADP through about pick 9 (the 1/2 turn), then by the window's projection from about pick 10 on
T2-1.name: T2 split at the 1/2 turn

T5-2.idea: T5 by the window's projection to the whole point, the less drafted first within the same point (VALUE first and PRICEY last kept)
T5-2.why: Jon, 2026-11-10: after the VALUE players T5 should go by projection, then reverse ADP within a projection; the late (under 50% drafted) players treated as level on ADP, the less drafted first among them. Tested before: projection straight lost to the button (AM -5.4 per pair, 228 pairs; PM -1.9, 542) and projection with ADP within 3 points had no lean (AM -1.6, 92; PM -0.8, 284); never tested: the less drafted first within a whole point. Contest side: PM T5 by ADP leans against (lift 0.80), the less-drafted tiebreak is a money RULE for

test.rule: Inside T5 at a window's record (projection: ours in AM, ETR in PM; drafted%: the window's): for two players in the same flag group (VALUE first and PRICEY last kept as the button), the one with the higher projection rounded to the whole point goes first; at the same whole point, the less drafted goes first (which also orders the under-50%-drafted players among themselves); with drafted% equal or missing, the button's order. Graded on 6-drafter decision pairs (ADP within 4) inside T5 that it orders differently from the button; a scratch scored through his swap; positive = the idea beat the button. A PM Questionable player pushed into T5 is left out, as for every idea.
test.backtest: The shadow's season line (in sample, every night before 2026-11-11), each window apart; the forward nights decide.
